# Foreign-consumer acceptance: managed loGo/s shared library.
# The library is built with the existing Go-syntax .lgo import-C export
# bridge. core.lgo holds Logos-only syntax (? on genuine foreign input);
# c_bridge.lgo is Go syntax only, per the rule pinned in logos_cgo_lgo.txt.
# The embedded C consumer compiles against ONLY the generated header and
# exercises every export from real C threads; the Python ctypes consumer
# repeats the same interface with full argtypes/restype.

[!cgo] skip 'cgo is not available'
[!buildmode:c-shared] stop
[GOOS:windows] skip 'POSIX sh/cc/pthreads consumer'

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env CGO_ENABLED=1

# Default CC: a host compiler setting must not drive the build.
env CC=

# Real managed shared library through the existing bridge and the
# standard c-shared mode. No new flag, generator, or second pipeline.
logos build -buildvcs=false -buildmode=c-shared -o $WORK/liblogos.so ./lib

# c-shared installs the generated C header next to the library.
exists $WORK/liblogos.so
exists $WORK/liblogos.h

# Real C consumer: fixed-width scalars, borrowed buffers (normal, empty,
# malformed, unconvertible length), error/panic statuses, handle
# lifecycle, and concurrent immutable-handle reads from foreign threads.
# Deletion happens after every thread joins, never racing use.
exec sh c/compile.sh $WORK
exec $WORK/consumer
stdout 'C-OK add=42 div=7 sum=42'

# Same C interface through Python ctypes. Conditional in the portable
# suite; acceptance hosts run it and observe PY-OK.
[exec:python3] exec python3 py/consumer.py $WORK
[exec:python3] stdout 'PY-OK add=42 sum=42 div=7 handle=7'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/shared

go 1.27

-- logos.toml --
[build]
cgo = "allow"

-- lib/core.lgo --
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// Counter is an immutable value object shared with foreign callers
// through an opaque handle. It is created once by LogosCounterNew and
// never mutated, so concurrent readers need no locking.
type Counter struct {
	seed int64
}

// NewCounter captures the foreign-supplied seed in an immutable value.
func NewCounter(seed int64) *Counter {
	return &Counter{seed: seed}
}

// Seed reports the captured value.
func (c *Counter) Seed() int64 {
	return c.seed
}

const (
	maxInt64 = int64(^uint64(0) >> 1)
	minInt64 = -maxInt64 - 1
)

// AddChecked adds two fixed-width integers, reporting overflow as an
// error instead of wrapping.
func AddChecked(a, b int64) (int64, error) {
	if (b > 0 && a > maxInt64-b) || (b < 0 && a < minInt64-b) {
		return 0, errors.New("logos: int64 overflow")
	}
	return a + b, nil
}

// Div is Go integer division. A zero divisor panics; the cgo bridge
// contains that panic and reports it instead of crashing the host.
func Div(a, b int64) int64 {
	return a / b
}

// SumPairText parses a borrowed "a,b" decimal field pair and sums it.
// The ? operator propagates genuine foreign-input failures as errors:
// empty, missing-comma, non-decimal, and overflowing inputs all fail
// here. No integer ever round-trips through text to exercise syntax.
func SumPairText(s string) (int64, error) {
	fields := strings.SplitN(s, ",", 2)
	if len(fields) != 2 {
		return 0, errors.New("logos: pair needs two comma-separated fields")
	}
	a := strconv.ParseInt(fields[0], 10, 64)?
	b := strconv.ParseInt(fields[1], 10, 64)?
	sum := AddChecked(a, b)?
	return sum, nil
}

-- lib/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
*/
import "C"

import (
	"runtime/cgo"
	"unsafe"
)

// Foreign status codes. One C interface reports every outcome:
//
//	0  ok
//	1  caller-visible error: bad input, overflow, or a length that
//	   cannot convert to int (checked before any slice is formed)
//	2  contained core panic (for example integer divide by zero);
//	   the host process survives
//	3  invalid or released handle; never aborts the host
//
// No managed pointer escapes into the foreign caller. Borrowed buffers
// are copied into Go before use and never retained. Results travel out
// only through caller-owned scalar slots.
//
// Concurrency contract: a Counter is immutable after LogosCounterNew
// returns, so concurrent LogosCounterGet calls on one handle are safe.
// LogosCounterDelete must happen after the last use; the caller joins
// every thread holding the handle first, so deletion never races use.
// A deleted or never-issued handle reports status 3.
//
// Caller preconditions (not runtime-validated; foreign addresses cannot
// be audited from Go): out slots are non-null writable scalars, and buf
// is non-null and readable for n bytes whenever n > 0. A null buf with
// n == 0 is the defined empty input.
const (
	logosOK        C.int32_t = 0
	logosErr       C.int32_t = 1
	logosPanic     C.int32_t = 2
	logosBadHandle C.int32_t = 3
)

// maxInt bounds int on this platform; a foreign length above it cannot
// back a slice and fails before unsafe.Slice runs.
const maxInt = int(^uint(0) >> 1)

//export LogosAdd
func LogosAdd(a, b C.int64_t, out *C.int64_t) C.int32_t {
	sum, err := AddChecked(int64(a), int64(b))
	if err != nil {
		return logosErr
	}
	*out = C.int64_t(sum)
	return logosOK
}

//export LogosDiv
func LogosDiv(a, b C.int64_t, out *C.int64_t) (res C.int32_t) {
	defer func() {
		if recover() != nil {
			res = logosPanic
		}
	}()
	*out = C.int64_t(Div(int64(a), int64(b)))
	return logosOK
}

//export LogosSumPair
func LogosSumPair(buf *C.char, n C.size_t, out *C.int64_t) (res C.int32_t) {
	defer func() {
		if recover() != nil {
			res = logosPanic
		}
	}()
	if uint64(n) > uint64(maxInt) {
		return logosErr
	}
	// Zero length is the defined empty input: no slice is formed, so
	// the empty path never depends on nil-pointer slice semantics.
	var raw []byte
	if n != 0 {
		raw = unsafe.Slice((*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(buf)), int(n))
	}
	sum, err := SumPairText(string(raw))
	if err != nil {
		return logosErr
	}
	*out = C.int64_t(sum)
	return logosOK
}

//export LogosCounterNew
func LogosCounterNew(seed C.int64_t, out *C.uintptr_t) C.int32_t {
	*out = C.uintptr_t(cgo.NewHandle(NewCounter(int64(seed))))
	return logosOK
}

//export LogosCounterGet
func LogosCounterGet(h C.uintptr_t, out *C.int64_t) C.int32_t {
	seed, ok := counterSeed(h)
	if !ok {
		return logosBadHandle
	}
	*out = C.int64_t(seed)
	return logosOK
}

//export LogosCounterDelete
func LogosCounterDelete(h C.uintptr_t) (res C.int32_t) {
	defer func() {
		if recover() != nil {
			res = logosBadHandle
		}
	}()
	cgo.Handle(h).Delete()
	return logosOK
}

// counterSeed resolves h through the runtime handle table only. There
// is no second registry: an unknown, zero, or already-deleted handle
// panics inside Value and fails closed here as ok == false.
func counterSeed(h C.uintptr_t) (seed int64, ok bool) {
	defer func() {
		if recover() != nil {
			ok = false
		}
	}()
	seed = cgo.Handle(h).Value().(*Counter).Seed()
	return seed, true
}

func main() {}

-- c/consumer.c --
// C consumer for the loGo/s c-shared foreign-consumer proof. Compiles
// against ONLY the generated liblogos.h plus system headers, links the
// built .so, and exercises every export: fixed-width scalars, borrowed
// buffers (normal, empty, malformed, unconvertible length), error and
// panic statuses, and the opaque-handle lifecycle. Eight pthreads read
// one immutable handle concurrently; the handle is deleted only after
// every thread joins, so deletion never races use. Any failure prints
// FAIL and exits nonzero; success prints C-OK.
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>

#include "liblogos.h"

static int failures = 0;

#define CHECK(cond)                                                      \
	do {                                                             \
		if (!(cond)) {                                           \
			printf("FAIL %s:%d: %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__,  \
			    #cond);                                  \
			failures = 1;                                \
		}                                                        \
	} while (0)

struct readers {
	uintptr_t handle;
	int64_t expect;
	int iters;
};

static void *read_loop(void *arg) {
	struct readers *r = (struct readers *)arg;
	for (int i = 0; i < r->iters; i++) {
		int64_t v = 0;
		int32_t st = LogosCounterGet(r->handle, &v);
		if (st != 0 || v != r->expect) {
			printf("FAIL foreign-thread read: st=%d v=%lld want %lld\n",
			    (int)st, (long long)v, (long long)r->expect);
			return (void *)1;
		}
	}
	return (void *)0;
}

int main(void) {
	int64_t v = 0;
	int32_t st = 0;

	st = LogosAdd(40, 2, &v);
	CHECK(st == 0 && v == 42);

	st = LogosAdd(9223372036854775807LL, 1, &v);
	CHECK(st == 1);

	st = LogosDiv(42, 6, &v);
	CHECK(st == 0 && v == 7);

	/* Zero divisor panics in Go; the bridge contains it and the host lives. */
	st = LogosDiv(1, 0, &v);
	CHECK(st == 2);

	const char *pair = "40,2";
	st = LogosSumPair((char *)pair, 4, &v);
	CHECK(st == 0 && v == 42);

	/* Empty input: null with zero length is defined, and fails as input error. */
	st = LogosSumPair((char *)0, 0, &v);
	CHECK(st == 1);

	st = LogosSumPair((char *)"x,2", 3, &v);
	CHECK(st == 1);

	st = LogosSumPair((char *)"7,", 2, &v);
	CHECK(st == 1);

	/* A length that cannot convert to int fails before any slice forms. */
	st = LogosSumPair((char *)pair, (uintptr_t)-1, &v);
	CHECK(st == 1);

	uintptr_t h = 0;
	st = LogosCounterNew(7, &h);
	CHECK(st == 0 && h != 0);

	v = 0;
	st = LogosCounterGet(h, &v);
	CHECK(st == 0 && v == 7);

	enum { NTHREADS = 8, ITERS = 1000 };
	pthread_t th[NTHREADS];
	struct readers r = { h, 7, ITERS };
	int ncreated = 0;
	for (int i = 0; i < NTHREADS; i++) {
		if (pthread_create(&th[i], 0, read_loop, &r) != 0) {
			CHECK(0);
			break;
		}
		ncreated++;
	}
	for (int i = 0; i < ncreated; i++) {
		void *rv = 0;
		CHECK(pthread_join(th[i], &rv) == 0 && rv == 0);
	}
	CHECK(ncreated == NTHREADS);

	v = 0;
	st = LogosCounterGet(h, &v);
	CHECK(st == 0 && v == 7);

	st = LogosCounterDelete(h);
	CHECK(st == 0);

	/* Released handles fail through the documented status, never abort. */
	st = LogosCounterGet(h, &v);
	CHECK(st == 3);
	st = LogosCounterDelete(h);
	CHECK(st == 3);

	if (failures == 0) {
		printf("C-OK add=42 div=7 sum=42 readers=%d iters=%d handle=7\n",
		    NTHREADS, ITERS);
	}
	return failures;
}

-- c/compile.sh --
#!/bin/sh
# Compile the C consumer against the generated c-shared header.
# Arg 1 is $WORK: the library lives at $1/liblogos.so with the header
# $1/liblogos.h beside it. Sources are relative to the script dir.
set -e
W="$1"
CCBIN=""
for c in cc gcc clang; do
	if command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		CCBIN="$c"
		break
	fi
done
if [ -z "$CCBIN" ]; then
	echo "no C compiler on PATH" >&2
	exit 1
fi
exec "$CCBIN" -std=c23 -o "$W/consumer" c/consumer.c -I"$W" -L"$W" -llogos "-Wl,-rpath,$W" -pthread

-- py/consumer.py --
"""Python ctypes consumer for the loGo/s c-shared proof.

Exercises the same generated C interface as the C consumer: normal,
error, empty, and lifecycle paths with full argtypes/restype. Every
check asserts a real status or value; an invalid handle must report
status 3 without aborting the host.
"""
import ctypes
import os
import sys

work = sys.argv[1]
lib = ctypes.CDLL(os.path.join(work, "liblogos.so"))

OK, ERR, PANIC, BAD_HANDLE = 0, 1, 2, 3

lib.LogosAdd.argtypes = (
    ctypes.c_int64, ctypes.c_int64, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int64))
lib.LogosAdd.restype = ctypes.c_int32

lib.LogosDiv.argtypes = (
    ctypes.c_int64, ctypes.c_int64, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int64))
lib.LogosDiv.restype = ctypes.c_int32

lib.LogosSumPair.argtypes = (
    ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int64))
lib.LogosSumPair.restype = ctypes.c_int32

lib.LogosCounterNew.argtypes = (
    ctypes.c_int64, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_size_t))
lib.LogosCounterNew.restype = ctypes.c_int32

lib.LogosCounterGet.argtypes = (
    ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int64))
lib.LogosCounterGet.restype = ctypes.c_int32

lib.LogosCounterDelete.argtypes = (ctypes.c_size_t,)
lib.LogosCounterDelete.restype = ctypes.c_int32


def main():
    out = ctypes.c_int64()
    # Normal scalar path.
    assert lib.LogosAdd(40, 2, ctypes.byref(out)) == OK
    assert out.value == 42
    # Error paths: overflow and malformed buffer.
    assert lib.LogosAdd(2**63 - 1, 1, ctypes.byref(out)) == ERR
    assert lib.LogosSumPair(b"40,2", 4, ctypes.byref(out)) == OK
    assert out.value == 42
    assert lib.LogosSumPair(b"x,2", 3, ctypes.byref(out)) == ERR
    # Empty input: NULL with zero length.
    assert lib.LogosSumPair(None, 0, ctypes.byref(out)) == ERR
    # Panic containment: the host survives divide by zero.
    assert lib.LogosDiv(1, 0, ctypes.byref(out)) == PANIC
    assert lib.LogosDiv(42, 6, ctypes.byref(out)) == OK
    assert out.value == 7
    # Lifecycle: create, use, delete, then released fails closed.
    handle = ctypes.c_size_t(0)
    assert lib.LogosCounterNew(7, ctypes.byref(handle)) == OK
    assert handle.value != 0
    assert lib.LogosCounterGet(handle, ctypes.byref(out)) == OK
    assert out.value == 7
    assert lib.LogosCounterDelete(handle) == OK
    assert lib.LogosCounterGet(handle, ctypes.byref(out)) == BAD_HANDLE
    assert lib.LogosCounterDelete(handle) == BAD_HANDLE
    print("PY-OK add=42 sum=42 div=7 handle=7")


main()
